description: Stripping the activity glyph cmux prints between a workspace ref and its title. Exactly one leading character is removed, then surrounding spaces are trimmed, when that character is a single scalar in the Braille Patterns block (U+2800–U+28FF, cmux's spinner frames) or the Dingbats block (U+2700–U+27BF: ✳ ✓ ✗ …) without emoji presentation. Everything else is returned verbatim: colour emoji (including emoji-presentation Dingbats like ✅ ✨ ❌ and any glyph followed by VS16), the leading … cmux prints on truncated path titles, other symbols, and any glyph that is not first. Cosmetic only: targeting uses the ref.
function: RemoteControlService.stripStatusGlyph(_:) — title string in, title string out
verifiedBy: Characterization of the Swift implementation (spec #93, ticket #121); Tests/PowerUpTests/CmuxReportingFixtureTests.swift. Emoji presentation follows the Unicode Emoji_Presentation property as reported by Swift's Unicode.Scalar.Properties.
capturedAgainst: cmux 0.64.17 (97) [9ed29d81a]; PowerUp macOS app, branch stage-1-text-views-spikes, 2026-10-23

cases.name: empty input
cases.reason: An empty title stays empty.

cases.name: plain title untouched
cases.reason: Titles without a glyph must arrive unchanged.

cases.name: Braille spinner frame U+2810 with space
cases.reason: cmux's activity spinner uses Braille Patterns; the frame is noise in a picker.

cases.name: Braille spinner frame U+280B
cases.reason: Every spinner frame is stripped, not just one.

cases.name: Braille spinner frame U+2839
cases.reason: Every spinner frame is stripped, not just one.

cases.name: Braille block lower bound U+2800
cases.reason: The blank Braille cell is a spinner frame too; it must not leave an invisible prefix.

cases.name: Braille block upper bound U+28FF
cases.reason: The full Braille range is treated as spinner frames.

cases.name: Dingbat eight-spoked asterisk U+2733
cases.reason: cmux's idle/attention mark; text-presentation Dingbat.

cases.name: Dingbat check mark U+2713
cases.reason: cmux's finished mark.

cases.name: Dingbat heavy check mark U+2714
cases.reason: Text-presentation Dingbat is a status mark.

cases.name: Dingbat ballot X U+2717
cases.reason: cmux's failure mark.

cases.name: Dingbat block lower bound U+2700
cases.reason: The full Dingbats block is treated as status marks.

cases.name: glyph glued to the title
cases.reason: cmux sometimes prints no space after the glyph.

cases.name: glyph followed by several spaces
cases.reason: All padding after the glyph goes with it.

cases.name: glyph alone
cases.reason: A row whose only title is the glyph shows as untitled.

cases.name: only one glyph is removed
cases.reason: Exactly one leading glyph is stripped, so anything after it is the user's own title.

cases.name: trailing spaces trimmed only when a glyph was stripped
cases.reason: Stripping trims the remainder.

cases.name: trailing spaces kept when there is no glyph
cases.reason: Without a glyph the title is returned verbatim (the parser trims before calling).

cases.name: leading space before a glyph is not stripped
cases.reason: Only a glyph in the very first position counts; the parser trims before calling.

cases.name: glyph in the middle not stripped
cases.reason: Only a leading glyph is a status mark; one inside the title is the user's text.

cases.name: Dingbat in the middle not stripped
cases.reason: Only a leading glyph is a status mark.

cases.name: emoji rocket preserved
cases.reason: A colour emoji is the user's own title decoration, not a status glyph.

cases.name: emoji-presentation Dingbat U+2705 preserved
cases.reason: U+2705 sits in the Dingbats block but has emoji presentation, so it is the user's emoji.

cases.name: emoji-presentation Dingbat U+2728 preserved
cases.reason: Sparkles is in Dingbats but renders as emoji; it must survive.

cases.name: emoji-presentation Dingbat U+274C preserved
cases.reason: Cross mark is in Dingbats but renders as emoji; it must survive.

cases.name: Dingbat with variation selector 16 preserved
cases.reason: With VS16 the glyph is an explicit emoji (two scalars, one character), so it is the user's.

cases.name: leading ellipsis preserved
cases.reason: cmux truncates path titles with U+2026; stripping it would show a plausible absolute path that does not exist.

cases.name: glyph then ellipsis keeps the ellipsis
cases.reason: Only the glyph goes; the truncation ellipsis after it stays.

cases.name: black star U+2605 preserved
cases.reason: Miscellaneous Symbols are not cmux status marks; the broad symbol categories are deliberately not stripped.

cases.name: bullet preserved
cases.reason: General punctuation that could start a title is not a status mark.

cases.name: quote preserved
cases.reason: A title may legitimately start with a quote.

cases.name: CJK after glyph
cases.reason: Non-Latin titles survive stripping intact.
